newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 6.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is facing serious internal party dissent in his plans to pave a way towards Greek-Turkish dialogue. Despite Simitis's assurances that Greece would not be negotiating its sovereign rights and that the move was a diplomatic response to international pressure, a number of ruling party PASOK members called for the issue to be discussed by the party, as it was "a change of policy".

--A former minister and another 32 members of the Political Spring party yesterday defected back to the conservative opposition New Democracy, sounding the warning bells for Political Spring leader Antonis Samaras.

--The winds of change are reportedly blowing through the Greek public service with the government considering the 15 billion drachma bill for air-conditioning, heating and light excessive. It's considering placing private-sector managers in control of "energy responsibility".
--More revelations from the papers of former president Constantine Karamanlis reveal the role played by Greece's ex-king Constantine in the days of the military dictatorship as well as after.
--In an effort to neutralise comments by pro-royalists in the New Democracy party ranks, party leader Costas Karamanlis yesterday blamed the government for stoking the fire.

--Mikis Theodorakis, the composer of "Zorba the Greek", cut short a European concert tour and returned to Athens yesterday after taking ill in Berlin. Doctors have ordered him to rest and stop smoking.
--New information from a Greek prisoner is leading police and Interpol to Germany where young Ben Needham, abducted from Greece in 1991, is reportedly living with a Greek migrant couple.
--Tony Blair, Britain's new prime minister, has adopted the heritage of Lord Elgin, with Britain's prompt refusal to return the Elgin Marbles to Greece.
--The sun took centre stage yesterday as Greenpeace demonstrated how solar energy can fuel a jazz concert, at a three-day conference on renewable energy in Athens.
--Athenians flooded the Organisation for Workers Housing yesterday as news got out that the organisation was offering rent subsidies.
